name: Rosuvastatin
sections: White amorphous powder (calcium salt), sparingly soluble in water.

The JUPITER trial (2008) showed a 44% reduction in major CV events in people with normal LDL but raised hs-CRP. Generics available from 2016. First approval/introduction: Discovered by Shionogi; patented 1991; US FDA August 2003 (AstraZeneca).

Competitive inhibitor of HMG-CoA reductase, the rate-limiting enzyme of cholesterol synthesis; up-regulates hepatic LDL receptors, lowering LDL-C (up to ~55% at 20 mg), triglycerides and raising HDL-C. Pleiotropic plaque-stabilising effects. Receptor / target profile: Potent competitive HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor; hydrophilic and hepatoselective (OATP1B1 uptake).
Limited (~10%), mainly CYP2C9 to N-desmethyl rosuvastatin
Summary: Bioavailability ~20%; Tmax 3–5 h. ~90% protein bound. Minimal metabolism (CYP2C9). Half-life ~19 h. Mainly faecal excretion. Asian patients have ~2-fold higher exposure.

JUPITER (Ridker et al., NEJM 2008) – 44% reduction in major CV events in people with raised hs-CRP.

Store below 30°C in a dry place, protected from light and moisture. Keep out of the reach of children. Do not use after the expiry date.
